newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan DIC to ask BOJ to cover account shortages.
newsitem.headline: Japan DIC to ask BOJ to cover account shortages.

text.p: Japan's Deposit Insurance Corp (DIC) will ask the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to cover any fund shortages in special accounts created to help cope with future financial failures, financial sources said on Friday.
If the DIC is unable to pay back the loans, financial institutions would be asked to lend to it for the purpose, the sources said.
Under financial bills passed by parliament in June, the special DIC accounts were created to protect depositors from possible financial failures over the next five years.
The new laws were aimed at helping to solve Japan's bad loan mess and boosted insurance premiums paid by financial institutions to DIC to 0.084 percent of total deposits from this financial year.
A premium equivalent to 0.036 percent of deposits goes to the special accounts.
About one trillion yen is available to the special accounts over the next five years. The new measure is to provide stopgap funds as the premiums are to be paid in installments, the sources said.

"The repayment of the funds (to financial institutions) is promised and lending to the DIC is done via auction and banks don't have to join in if they don't want to," one financial source said. "This is a scheme to make up temporarily for any shortage in the special funds."
Another source said the DIC would likely be forced to boost the premiums again in order to deal with any future financial failures.
